description: Catalog every data set under roots into index_dir (Parquet: one row per data set with format, size, sample, instrument, technique, method, operator, start, dimensions, channels, objective, events, scans, integrity status, personal-data flags). Headers only and resumable: a call stops after max_files/max_seconds with complete=false, and the same call again continues. openreadout_search queries the result. For one folder of files, openreadout_batch with measure info lists what each file is in one call.

check.description: Integrity check per data set: `headers` (default; structure only), `full` or `none`.

exclude.description: Glob patterns of names or root-relative paths to skip.

follow_symlinks.description: Crawl directories behind symbolic links too (links to files are always read).

full_rescan.description: Read every file again instead of reusing unchanged records.

index_dir.description: Index directory to create or update (never inside a root).

max_files.description: Stop after this many files in this call (default 20000); call again to continue.

max_seconds.description: Stop after this many seconds in this call (default 45); call again to continue.

restart.description: Discard an interrupted crawl instead of resuming it.

threads.description: Worker threads (default: the number of CPUs).

name: openreadout_index

CrawlStats.description: Counters of one crawl (cumulative over resumed sessions of the same run).

bytes_read.description:
Bytes the crawler itself read (sniffing and fingerprints); the readers' own header reads
are not counted.

changed.description: Items read again (size, time or tool version changed).

elapsed_s.description: Wall time of the crawl, seconds (all sessions of a resumed run).

files_seen.description: Files seen, counting every file inside directory data sets.

items.description: Walk items processed: files and directory data sets.

new.description: Items read for the first time.

recognised.description: Items a reader recognised (before multi-file grouping).

removed.description: Items of the previous run that are gone.

sessions.description: Sessions this run took (1 plus the number of resumes).

unchanged.description: Items reused from the previous run without being opened.

unreadable.description: Recognised items that could not be opened or summarized.

IndexSettings.description: Crawl options that shape the index.

datasets_flagged.description: Data sets with at least one flag.

columns.description:
Columns (name, type, unit class, description). Always in `index.json`; left out of the
MCP tool's answer (listed in `index.json` and `book/src/guides/lab-shares.md`).

file.description: File name inside the index directory.

Tally.description: A count and a byte total.

ToolInfo.description: The tool that wrote the index.

WalkStats.description: Counters of what the walk skipped.

excluded.description: Entries skipped by `--exclude` (and the index directory).

symlinks_skipped.description: Symbolic links to directories skipped (not followed).

unreadable_directories.description: Directories that could not be listed.

complete.description:
True when the crawl walked every root to the end. False after a cap (`--max-files`,
`--max-seconds`) or an interruption: the tables then hold what was read so far plus the
previous run's records for the rest, and rerunning the same command continues.

crawl.description: Crawl counters, cumulative over resumed sessions.

datasets.description: Data sets (rows of `experiments.parquet`) after multi-file grouping.

families.description: Data sets and bytes per family.

files_per_s.description: Items per second over the crawl's wall time.

formats.description: Data sets and bytes per format id.

index_dir.description: Absolute path of the index directory.

next.description: What to do next, when the crawl is not complete.

tool.description: The tool and version that wrote it.

unknown_extensions.description: Files no reader recognises, per lower-case extension (`(none)` for no extension).

years.description: Data sets per acquisition year (`unknown` when the file records no date).
